article.title: Israeli military detains Egyptian national who crossed border
article.summary:
Egyptian man held after crossing into Israel near Nitzana, his motive for the crossing still unknown.
Israel’s military has said that it detained an Egyptian civilian overnight after he crossed a border fence from Egyptian territory into Israel near Nitzana and that he was transferred to security forces for further questioning.
Nitzana is a small community in southern Israel’s western Negev (Naqab) Desert, sitting directly adjacent to the Egyptian border opposite the Egyptian side’s Al-Awja area.
The Nitzana border crossing, also known as the Eliav crossing, primarily handles cargo transport between the two countries rather than serving as a major passenger channel.
The incident occurred as Israel maintains heightened alert levels along the Egyptian border.

article.title: Syria-Jordan border reopens amid probe into deadly air strikes
article.summary:
Foreign ministers form security committee to share intelligence and follow up on impact of Jordan’s strikes on Syria.
Syria is reopening its border crossing with Jordan, and the two countries will investigate Jordanian strikes on suspected ISIL (ISIS) sites that killed seven in southern Syria.
Jordan’s strikes on Syria killed at least seven people in Deraa and Suwayda, including five members of the same family, three of whom were children.
Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi said Monday’s air attacks were based on field intelligence and aimed at “neutralising confirmed threats and imminent terrorist operations targeting Jordan’s security”.
Jordanian security forces arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law on suspicion of carrying out the attack.

article.title: What Vucic’s defeat means for Serbia’s foreign policy
article.summary:
As Belgrade prepares for a turbulent transition and the upcoming presidential elections in December, international observers and regional neighbours have been asking whether Vucic’s departure will prompt a shift in Serbia’s foreign policy.
Serbia’s relations with Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro and Kosovo have often been frayed by Vucic’s nationalistic rhetoric.
Of all elements of Serbian public policy, foreign policy will transform the least under the forthcoming governmental changes, Vuk Vuksanovic, a lecturer in foreign policy at King’s College London, predicted to Al Jazeera.
Bosko Jaksic, a foreign policy analyst, told Al Jazeera that while ties will not be severed, recent controversial agreements will face scrutiny.
Multiple chairsLooking at the broader geopolitical alignment, he emphasised that Serbia’s foreign policy will inevitably undergo a review.

article.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
article.summary:
A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources.
Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity.
On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous.
However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported.
US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.

article.title: Egyptian parliament authorises military aid for Saudi Arabia
article.summary:
Legislators approve military support amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, but Cairo has ruled out strikes on Yemen.
Egypt’s parliament has authorised President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia as attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis intensify.
A parliamentary statement shared with the Reuters news agency said el-Sisi had been authorised to “undertake necessary” measures to support Saudi Arabia in defending itself, should Riyadh request assistance.
It follows Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s international airport and facilities belonging to Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, Aramco, disrupting flights and oil exports.
The vote followed closed-door parliamentary discussions and an earlier postponement of the military aid authorisation for Saudi Arabia, which is one of Egypt’s most important economic partners.

article.title: Results trickling in after Israel's election shine a light on a complex political system
article.summary:
JERUSALEM (AP) — Israel was counting votes Wednesday in pivotal elections where no clear winner emerged in exit polls — a scenario that is shining a light on the country's complex political system.
Exit polls suggested Netanyahu's opponents had secured enough seats to form a government.
Israelis vote for parties and not candidates, and no single party has ever won an outright 61-seat majority in the Knesset, meaning political leaders must forge coalitions to govern.
Israeli broadcasters release exit pollsShortly after polls closed Tuesday at 10 p.m., Israel's three main television broadcasters released exit polls estimating how many seats were won by each party.
The exit polls usually provide a good indication of how people have voted.

article.title: US government acting illegally over electronic surveillance of its own citizens, say senators
article.summary:
Two senators with notable expertise in intelligence matters say that the US government is acting illegally over electronic surveillance of its own citizens.
They say the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) has permitted intelligence agencies to continue warrantless interception of messages by US citizens despite failing to comply with the administration’s own privacy promise to allow public review of such rulings …The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) was supposed to allow interception of communications by agents of foreign powers on US soil.
Controversially, however, it has also been used to intercept the communications of American citizens without a warrant under a clause known as Section 702.
Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires.
Wyden is the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff formerly chaired the equivalent House committee.

article.title: Why India has soured on Trump ahead of US midterms
article.summary:
Seven years after Modi backed Trump, analysts say New Delhi may now hope US midterm losses leave the president chastened.
Share Why India has soured on Trump ahead of US midterms on social mediaNew Delhi, India – Standing next to United States President Donald Trump, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered praise after praise.
Modi even borrowed a line from his own successful election campaigns, saying: “Abki baar, Trump sarkaar!”, Hindi for “This time, a Trump government.”But Trump lost.
Far from endorsing Trump, Indian officials have in recent weeks been more direct than ever in their criticism of his administration, amid a series of setbacks to bilateral ties.
